text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementNeuroscienceCan Psychedelics Improve Decision-making?A new study suggests they free the mind from prior biasesJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CST on November 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIn 1972, Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Dock Ellis pitched a no-hitter against the San Diego Padres. It’s an impressive feat on its own, but Ellis, under the mistaken assumption he had the day off, had taken a couple hits of LSD before the game. Completely zonked on acid, he managed to last through nine scoreless innings, leading his team to a 2-0 victory. Is it possible the drugs helped? Well, a new study published in Science Advances suggests psychedelics could lead to better decision-making (at least in mice). Powered By 10 ShareNextStayTo investigate the link between psychedelic drugs and decision-making, a team of Boston University neuroscientists put laboratory mice through a simple test. The lab animals were offered three holes, poking their noses through the center one kicked the experiment off. The other two holes had blinking lights that flashed either quickly or slowly, a nose poke in the fast-flashing hole earned the rodents a sugary reward. Read more: “The Promise and Peril of Toad Smoking, the Everest of Psychedelics”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
